title: Pricing & Best Practices

body.text: Codex comes with paid ChatGPT plans (Plus/Pro/Team), and
usage quota depends on the plan
— large, complex tasks use more quota than small ones. Breaking a big job into smaller tasks controls both quality and quota better.

example: "Instead of 'rewrite the whole app' → split into 'extract the auth module' + 'extract payment' + 'extract UI', one task at a time"

title: Best-practices recap

body.text: write clear tasks · split into small jobs · review every diff · always have tests · never skip the review
— the AI gets better every day, but responsibility for the code is still yours.

example: "Course complete! Start with a small task in your real repo, like 'add tests for a function that doesn't have any'"

question: How should you handle a large, complex job?

options.text: Split it into several smaller tasks
Do it all in one command
Don't use Codex for big jobs

question: Which is a Codex best practice?

options.text: Always review every diff before approving

question: Who has final responsibility for code quality?

options.text: Us — the people who use and review the code

question: What's the best practice when using Codex?

options.text: Use the code immediately without checking
Write clear tasks, test, and review before using for real

question: What should you keep in mind about pricing?

options.text: It has nothing to do with usage
Use resources appropriately for the job
